ideas.pitch: An automated platform that spins up deliberately vulnerable web apps with dynamic CTF flags for beginner security students.
ideas.title: CTFLearns: Automated Vulnerability Lab Generator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the beginner-friendly focus of the hackathon by providing educational utility that judges and organizers can immediately use for future cohorts.

ideas.pitch: A defense-in-depth security proxy that intercepts and sanitizes prompt injections targeting AI agents used in CTF challenges.
ideas.title: PromptShield: Layered LLM Injection Hardening Sandbox
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages advanced security concepts proven in past wins like the BitGN Personal Agent Challenge winner, showing robust defensive engineering.

ideas.pitch: A Python-based CLI tool that parses network logs and terminal histories to automatically generate structured cybersecurity incident reports and CTF writeups.
ideas.title: SecReportr: Automated CTF Writeup & Security Insight Generator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the exact pattern of Microsoft's Global Intern Hackathon winner by automating documentation and security reporting workflows.

ideas.pitch: A BERT-powered local detection system for identifying sophisticated phishing emails, SMS, and malicious call scripts during security training labs.
ideas.title: PhishGuard: Multi-Vector Spam and Phishing Detector
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the success of the Cyber Hackathon runner-up by implementing practical machine learning models directly addressing everyday cybersecurity threats.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight edge-based packet analyzer that maps real-time network attacks onto an interactive graph for defensive security students.
ideas.title: AegisAgent: Edge Network Intrusion and Attack Visualizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines complex graph intelligence and edge resilience seen in top-tier winning projects into a beginner-accessible educational format.
